modes.name: unnecessary_escalation
modes.definition: The agent creates a human support ticket that achieves nothing. Present when escalate_to_human is called and no escalation requirement in SPEC.md section 5 applies, and the help center and the order record together contain what the answer needs. Also present when the ticket is redundant: a second ticket for a case that already has one, or a ticket opened alongside a refund that issue_refund has already queued for human approval under ESC-1. In both cases the case is already in front of a human and the extra ticket adds no remedy.
modes.boundary: Absent when the escalation is required: any escalation requirement in SPEC.md section 5 applies — currently an account change, a dispute whose 60-day window is still open, a case genuinely unresolvable from the help center and the order record, or genuine uncertainty about whether policy permits an action. Also absent when the agent does not escalate at all. A trace that faced the same situation and answered without escalating is a close negative. Judged per ticket, not per trace: a trace whose first escalation was required and whose second was redundant is present. A queued refund is already an escalation: ESC-1 is satisfied when issue_refund returns queued_for_approval, and the agent's job is to explain that result, so a ticket opened to get the refund reviewed is present. When the user asked for the refund and the refund review decides the whole case, a ticket beside it is secondary and present. The exception is a ticket that asks a human for something the refund review does not cover, such as investigating a dispute. A package marked delivered that the user never received is such a dispute, so its ticket is absent even beside a queued refund; the refund is the misstep there, and it belongs to another mode. Judged on whether the situation required the ticket, not on the reason the agent gives for it. A required ticket filed under a misstated reason, for example a refund-exception review on an order whose own record is inconsistent, is absent; the misstatement is a response failure, not this one. An order still in transit inside its expected delivery window has not gone missing yet; a ticket for it is present.

modes.name: internal_detail_exposed
modes.definition: The user-facing reply exposes an internal representation: a policy identifier (cw-* or store-*-policy) instead of the policy's public title, or a raw data field name or tool-result key such as refund_eligible.
modes.boundary: Absent when the reply cites the policy by its public title ("Cartwheel refund policy") and states record facts in plain language ("this order is not eligible for a refund"). An internal identifier appearing only inside a tool result, never in the reply, is absent.

modes.name: threshold_misapplied
modes.definition: The agent applies the $100 automatic-refund threshold to an order that never reaches the eligibility check, either as a reason to open a ticket or as an unsolicited remark. The threshold governs issue_refund's queueing for orders that pass eligibility; it has no bearing on an ineligible one.
modes.boundary: Absent when the order is refund-eligible and the reply explains that the refund was queued for human review, which is correct handling under ESC-1. Absent when the threshold is not mentioned. Nearest neighbour: unnecessary_escalation, which covers tickets opened for other unsupported reasons.

modes.name: store_override_missed
modes.definition: The agent applies or cites the platform return or refund policy on an order from a store whose own policy overrides it. Present when the reply states a window, a deadline, or an eligibility reason drawn from the platform default while a store override governs the order.
modes.boundary: Absent when the store has no override, because the platform policy is then the governing one — true even if the agent never verified it (support-0130). Absent when the reply reaches a verdict without citing or applying a window at all, which is appropriate when the user asked for a yes or no (support-0247). Absent when the reply states the store's own window. A wrong window is the trigger; failing to check is not, because a check leaves no trace in the reply when the platform default happens to govern.
modes.spec_note: Requirement now in SPEC.md; see analysis/report/spec_revisions.md for what changed and why.

modes.name: date_interval_error
modes.definition: The reply states a date, an elapsed interval, or a conflict between the user's account and the order record that is wrong given the world date of 2026-07-01.
modes.boundary: Absent when the arithmetic is right, including when the agent correctly identifies a genuine mismatch. Present whether or not the reply prints a number: asserting an order is outside a window it is inside counts, even when only the delivery date and the rule are shown. Nearest neighbour: store_override_not_checked, where the window was never established at all.

modes.name: irrelevant_policy_detail

modes.name: dispute_window_not_applied
modes.definition: Before escalating a money-back request the agent does not establish whether the 60-day dispute window is open. Present when it escalates on an order delivered more than 60 days ago, where neither the return nor the dispute window leaves a human anything to grant.
modes.boundary: A weak-reason escalation is unnecessary_escalation either way; the dispute window decides whether it is also this. Absent when the order was delivered 60 days ago or less, because the dispute window was still open and a human had something left to grant — a bad escalation, not a futile one (support-0242 at 31 days, support-0129 at 35). Absent when the escalation was routing a corrupted record rather than seeking a remedy, since a human can fix a broken record whatever the window says (support-0190, order 8003, store_mismatch). Absent when the agent does not escalate, or states the dispute position correctly. Not present merely for failing to volunteer the dispute route to a user who never raised one.

modes.name: data_quality_surfaced
modes.definition: The agent volunteers a corrupted catalogue value the user had not raised. Present when a reply introduces a defective value from shared data — a negative price, a blank or duplicated product title — that the user did not already know about, with or without a disclaimer, because the affected item should be omitted instead.
modes.boundary: Absent when the user has already found the bad data and is asking about it: answering honestly and escalating is the correct response, not a disclosure failure (support-0192, where the shopper says the price 'looks way too low to be real'). Absent when the corrupted datum belongs to the user, since a defect in their own order is explained and escalated under the revised RESP-3 (support-0181, 0182, 0190). Absent when the agent omits the affected item. Two things decide it: who owns the record, and who raised it first.
modes.spec_note: Requirement now in SPEC.md; see analysis/report/spec_revisions.md for what changed and why.

manual_assignments.why: Reviewer-assigned: the reply states the Rustic Pitcher price as -$5.00, a catalogue defect reaching the user. The open code on the trace was about wanting a defect-reporting channel, so text matching missed it.

Same defective order, escalated correctly. Moved out of the positives: it was flagged for misdescribing the mismatch, which is date_interval_error, not for surfacing it.
Order 8003, store mismatch. Routed to a human without exposing the corrupted store reference to the user. The quieter correct handling of an owned defect.

revisions.change: Re-derived on the ownership split introduced by the RESP-3 revision. support-0192 added as a positive, a catalogue defect the reply states as -$5.00. support-0182 moved to close negative: it is an order defect the agent escalated correctly, flagged only for misdescribing the mismatch. The criterion is now catalogue-only.

Narrowed from 'a corrupted catalogue value reaches the user' to 'the agent volunteers one the user had not raised'. Found while verifying support-0192 as a proposed positive: the shopper had already spotted the price and asked about it, so an honest answer is correct. Two independent tests now apply — record ownership, and who raised the defect first.

Searched the unreviewed store for a third positive and found none. support-0196 and 0200 had users who raised the defect themselves; support-0198 discloses to support staff, who are the escalation target; support-0203 is a merchant asking about their own store; support-0201 and 0202 handled or concealed it. Submitted with two positives and the population analysis recorded.

modes.positive_shortfall: Two confirmed positives rather than the three Part D asks for, and the search established there is no third in the 250-trace store. Of 15 catalogue-defect scenarios: 6 users had already spotted the defect and raised it, which is absent; 4 are merchants or support staff asking about data they own or are the escalation target for, also absent; 3 were handled correctly or concealed the defect instead of surfacing it. That leaves support-0191 and support-0199, both shoppers browsing, both told about a corrupted listing they never asked about. The shortfall is a property of the scenario set, not of the search: narrowing the mode by record ownership and by who raised the defect first is what reduced the population, and both narrowings were deliberate.

modes.name: internal_field_exposed
modes.definition: The user-facing reply contains a raw data field name or tool-result key, such as refund_eligible or delivered_at.
modes.boundary: Absent when the reply states the same fact in plain language ("this order is not eligible for a refund"). Distinct from internal_policy_id_cited: a fix that renders policy titles would not remove a field name.

grouping.note: A note may support more than one failure mode, and a trace may carry several. created_from and positive_traces are therefore overlapping sets, not a partition. Part E assigns one present/absent judgment per trace and mode pair.

close_negative_test: A close negative is useful only if a reasonable reviewer, applying the written definition, could get it wrong. It must sit where the definition is silent or ambiguous, not merely where the surface vocabulary matches. A trace the definition clearly decides is a plain negative and teaches nothing. Practical consequence: accepting a close negative should change the boundary text. If the boundary needs no edit afterwards, the trace was not close. Where a definition is tight enough that nothing is arguable, zero close negatives with the reason recorded is the honest answer, which the handout permits with 'when the reviewed data permits them'.

agentdebug_comparison.source: AgentErrorTaxonomy, Zhu et al., arXiv:2509.25370, 29 September 2025
agentdebug_comparison.modes_added: none — no addition was supported by our own traces and annotations

mapping.dispute_window_not_applied: Memory / Retrieval Failure plus Planning / Constraint Ignorance

agentdebug_comparison.structural_difference: Their 17 modes describe the agent's internal loop; nothing covers what reaches a person. Their benchmarks are ALFWorld, GAIA and WebShop, task environments with no customer. Four of our eight modes, including our largest at 56 traces, have no counterpart.
agentdebug_comparison.omission_identified: Memory. Three of their modes and most of Reflection concern multi-turn state, and we have 32 multi-turn conversations but only one open code touching it: support-0238, 'Did not address the order number confusion from previous turn', which is their Over-simplification or Retrieval Failure. One trace cannot support a mode, so none was added, but the gap may reflect under-sampling of multi-turn failures rather than their absence.
agentdebug_comparison.second_candidate: Planning / Inefficient Planning, for which we have two instances, support-0033 and support-0207, both 'too many tool calls'. Below the three-trace minimum.
agentdebug_comparison.convergence: Their critical error, 'the earliest step whose correction directly prevents the final failure', is functionally identical to the handout's first-failure stopping rule.

quick_fixes.title: Out-of-scope advice about using a purchased product
quick_fixes.requirement: SCOPE-2 (and RESP-4 for how to decline)
quick_fixes.what_happened: A shopper asked what else they could do with coffee beans bought on Cartwheel. The agent answered with 2,227 characters of recipes, headings and quantities. The scenario's own criterion is that the agent declines in one or two sentences and points to what it can help with.
quick_fixes.why_it_slipped: Three of the four out-of-scope traces in the store decline correctly — tax advice, a laptop recommendation, and a request for other customers' identities. Those are plainly outside Cartwheel. This one concerns a product the user actually bought here, which reads as in scope and is not: SCOPE-2 excludes general questions, and how to cook with a product is general advice.
quick_fixes.fix: State in the system prompt that a question about using, maintaining or repurposing a product is out of scope even when the product was bought on Cartwheel. The agent handles the order, the return, the refund and the policy; it does not advise on the item itself.
quick_fixes.not_a_failure_mode: One instance in 100 reviewed traces, and three of four comparable traces are handled correctly.

changes: SCOPE-2 now excludes advice about using a product bought on Cartwheel (support-0102).
ESC-1 says a queued refund is already with a human, so no ticket is opened alongside it (support-0211, 0046).
ESC-5 added: only ESC-1 to ESC-4 escalate; no duplicate tickets; no escalation once both windows have closed.

RESP-1 now requires the public title in user-facing text and excludes raw field names, while allowing identifiers the user can act on (support-0083 and 28 others; the Product ID question from Part C).
